CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Semarang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Human Rights is a set of rights inherent to the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and constitutes His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
9. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society.
10. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.

1.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines “Kekerasan Terhadap Perempuan” broadly as acts causing suffering “baik yang terjadi di ranah privat atau publik” (Art. 1(8)), and then regulates prevention/services for violence against women generally (Arts. 18–21). However, it never explicitly names or defines “kekerasan dalam rumah tangga” / domestic violence / household violence as a specific category. Mention of “ranah privat” is not the same as an explicit domestic-violence category. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the text shown, and the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be an over-inclusive label for this specific indicator.

1.10.evaluator_rationale: The prevention measures explicitly include education and advocacy directed at social media owners/managers/users, indicating attention to violence risks facilitated through digital/social media platforms.

NUMBER 7 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

d. right to perform work according to the determined time.
e. right to labor placement.
f. right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. right to obtain welfare through labor social security.
h. right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, obtain rest opportunity for a minimum of half an hour.
k. right to maternity leave, miscarriage and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers:
Female workers/laborers are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who experience miscarriage are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who during menstruation feel pain and notify the employer, are not obligated to work on the first and second day during menstruation.
l. right to perform worship.
m. right to conduct work strikes.
n. right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or dismissal.
o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

7.3.rationale: Funding sources are specified in Indonesian Art. 32: “bersumber dari: a. Anggaran Pendapatan dan Belanja Daerah; dan b. sumber lain yang sah dan tidak mengikat.” This does not explicitly mention international donors/donor funding. The judge relied instead on Art. 31(2)(e) about coordinating “bantuan internasional,” but that clause is in the guidance/supervision section and does not establish funding sources or donor financing. ‘International assistance’ could be technical support, cooperation, or other non-funding aid. Thus the judge’s ‘Yes’ is an overreach given the indicator is specifically about budget/funding sources (international donors), making this an evaluation failure (misuse of a non-budget clause as funding evidence).
